key_insight: STAR-XPC uses a permutation-invariant Set Transformer to predict X-ray transmission through polymer composites in milliseconds with high agreement to Monte Carlo simulations.
engineering_relevance: Rapid transmission estimates could accelerate screening of polymer-composite radiation shields while reducing reliance on costly transport simulations.
method: Embed molecular constituents with pretrained ChemBERTa.
Combine constituent embeddings, mass fractions, and four bulk descriptors in a Set Transformer supporting up to 11 constituents.
Train on automated PENELOPE/penEasy simulations of polyethylene-based slabs.
evidence_signal: Leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation on 4,697 simulated configurations achieved R² = 0.9988, MSE = (1.12 ± 0.56)×10⁻⁴, and median absolute percentage error of 1.15%.
watch_item: Performance beyond the simulated polyethylene-based composites, 0.15–2.5 mm thicknesses, and four tube voltages requires validation.
paper_title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
